answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. The result is a self-purifying economy: every epoch, low-cost fake identities are filtered out by the same reputation mechanics that reward the honest ones.. This works because the originality bar tightens as more low-quality answers appear, raising the per-alias cost of a coordinated fake campaign. Consider a ripple as the anchor of the cost.
